objects._comment: Object detection and wrist attribution. Off by default; --objects overrides. Which classes are detected comes from detector.classes above. Enabling this turns pose on implicitly, because attribution needs wrist keypoints.
objects._comment_margin: How far outside an object's box a wrist may be and still count as holding it, as a fraction of box size. Too tight and a phone held at arm's length is never attributed; too loose and a bottle on the desk is attributed to whoever walks past.
objects._comment_min_wrist_score: Attribution needs a wrist the pose model was reasonably sure about. In a webcam run where wrists averaged 0.30 with only 39% above threshold, a phone was seen 90 times and attributed 3 times -- the wrist, not the object, was the limiting factor.

pose._comment: RTMPose keypoint estimation. Off by default; enabled implicitly by objects or actions. Needs the exported model: python perception/tools/export_rtmpose.py
pose._comment_runtime: 'auto' prefers onnxruntime and falls back to cv2.dnn, which is roughly 4x slower.

actions._comment: PoseC3D action recognition. Off by default; --actions overrides. Needs the exported model: python perception/tools/export_posec3d.py. NOTE: action recognition needs the WHOLE BODY in frame. Hips and knees carry most of the signal and a laptop webcam at desk distance sees neither, which shows up as near-total abstention.
actions._comment_every_s: Seconds between inferences per track. PoseC3D costs ~130-185 ms and reads a ~2 s window, so running it per frame would re-analyse almost the same window at full price. This is a latency budget as much as a cost control: no action model can classify an action before it has happened.
actions._comment_classes: 'ntu60' is the stock checkpoint's vocabulary -- 'drink water', 'taking a selfie'. Nothing about workflows. Site classes mean replacing cls_head.fc_cls and fine-tuning; supply a list here once you have.
actions._comment_abstention: Both tests must pass or the result is an abstention, emitted as value 'unknown'. min_margin matters more than it looks: two classes at 0.41 and 0.39 is not a recognition, and on a real floor the confusable pairs are exactly the ones that matter.
